This was a stale-scope re-read of build 4 (f83e789..571ae37). The build touched only test-only code: internal/testutil/fakegithub/fakegithub.go and its test, internal/testutil/seeded/main.go, and the new seed.go and screens_test.go. No product file changed. site.css, every template, internal/layout, internal/auth, internal/server, routes, CSP and the iframe are byte-identical to f83e789, which my attempt 3 reviewed and found clean. Its measurements still stand for those files. What I checked in the new code: - OfferChoices turns the authorize endpoint into a picker drawn with html/template. Labels and hrefs are escaped. The picked index is checked, so out-of-range, negative and non-numeric picks get a 400. Every earlier refusal (client_id, redirect_uri, state, PKCE, scope) still fires before the picker. DenyAtAuthorize skips the picker. - Each code carries the chosen account into its token, and /user answers for that account. With no choices offered, the token's value is nil and /user reads SetUser's user at request time, exactly as before. - In run(), the launcher's stand-in is built and given its choices before program.Start binds n. Its redirect_uri equals Start's base plus /auth/github/callback. serveEnv overrides only the GitHub URLs, client id and secret through childEnv. HBAND_OWNER_GITHUB_ID still comes from Start. The cleanups run in LIFO order, so the program is killed before the fake closes. - seedScreens checks each step for a 303. - The six engine screens in the build's `screens` press "Continue as the owner" and "Continue as a reader". Those are exactly the seed.go constants ownerChoice and readerChoice. I read only that field of build-slice-4.json to check this contract. What I ran: - `go vet` on fakegithub and seeded is clean. - TestOfferChoicesMakesTheAuthorizePageAPicker and TestSeededProductOffersTheOwnerAndTheReader pass (3 subtests). - `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` with CHROME_BIN set exits 0. All 34 packages are ok, every tests/acceptance package included. - The engine's Fitness check holds all 45 rules. - gofmt -l on the committed blobs of the five Go files is clean. A scratch overlay probe measured one contract trap. The *program.Program that run() returns carries program.Start's own stand-in as its Fake, but the serving program talks to the launcher's stand-in. On that value, p.Owner(t) fatals with "not a redirect to GitHub's authorize page". No caller uses it today, so I filed it as an extra. Also filed: one half-migrated switch in userInfo (an extra) and two stale comments (text). Nothing sends the build back. Second reader, for inputs: Input pass over build 4 (f83e789..571ae37): the OfferChoices picker in the stand-in GitHub, seedScreens, and run(), which now serves through the launcher's own stand-in. I read all five changed Go files whole, along with program.Start, childEnv, SignIn and Approve. **Inputs that hold:** - The picker's labels and links are drawn by html/template. - A `pick` value that is not a choice ("2", "-1", "x") gets a 400. - A bad client_id gets a 400 while choices are on offer. - DenyAtAuthorize skips the picker. - A token carries a copy of the picked account, so a later SetUser cannot change who it signs in. - The launcher's stand-in has its redirect_uri set to `http://127.0.0.1:/auth/github/callback`, which is what HBAND_BASE_URL produces, and it is checked against port n. - On the reviewed tree, `go test -count=1` of ./internal/testutil/seeded, ./internal/testutil/fakegithub and ./internal/testutil/program passes. **Two defects, both confirmed by running scratch tests through `go test -overlay`:** 1. **fakegithub.userInfo uses the wrong ID under two switches.** It now answers with the picked account's id, login and avatar, but the UserIDString and UserIDFloat cases still format `f.user.ID`. A picked owner (4242) therefore comes back as id "42" or 42.0, the account SetUser names. The repro fails on 571ae37 and passes once both lines read `user.ID`. 2. **run() returns a Program whose Fake is the wrong stand-in.** The serving program redirects sign-in to the launcher's stand-in (port 52408 in my run), but the returned Program's Fake is a different one (52409), the stand-in program.Start made for itself, which nothing asks. A caller's p.Fake, p.SignIn, p.Owner and p.Approve on that Program therefore talk to the wrong stand-in. The repro fails today and passes once `final.Fake = fake` is set. TestSeededProductOffersTheOwnerAndTheReader and the rest of the seeded package still pass with that change. Nothing was written to the repository (git status is unchanged), and my scratch folder is removed. Reading pass: I read every range the engine listed, all with numbered Reads: internal/auth/forbidden_test.go 1-58, internal/auth/owner.go 1-100, forbidden.html 1-11, internal/layout/layout.go 1-16, layout_test.go 1-208 and base.html 1-17, comment_test.go 1077-1153, frame_test.go 1-99, reader.go 20-95, router.go 10-101, site.css 1-262, stylesheet_test.go 1-492, look_test.go 1-777, the three admin templates, all_reports.html, branch.html, layout.html and report.html 1-24. These files did not change in build 4 (f83e789..571ae37). Nothing in them is new to file. The shell contract holds: - base.html defines only head, page-start and page-end. page-start writes the thread.js tag only behind `{{if .ThreadScript}}` and then calls the consuming set's "header". - parsePages() parses layout.FS first and templateFS second, and newApp uses it. TestThreadTenThousandTiming changes only its setup line, to `pages := parsePages()`. - pageData.ThreadScript() returns false and readerData returns HasReport. - forbiddenPage is parsed from layout.FS and then forbidden.html, and executed with forbiddenData{forbiddenTitle, v.Login}. forbiddenData's ThreadScript is false. - RequireOwner's order, its Cache-Control and its plain-403 fallback are unchanged. - forbidden.html opens with page-start, closes with page-end and defines a header that holds only the brand. The templates match the plan: - report.html, branch.html and all_reports.html change only their shell lines. - The admin pages carry the .admin wrapper, admin-nav with its section dot, the page-head, the pills, the empty and empty-inline classes and the lede. - `

Nothing visible on this report.

` keeps its pinned markup, and site.css styles it through `.moderation > h2 + p:last-child`. - layout.html adds only the admin-nav define. site.css keeps line 1, the light-dark() token table, the hidden guard, every pinned rule text and the literal thread geometry. It writes edges as a literal width and style with a *-color longhand, and Canvas appears only in the iframe rule. The checkers in stylesheet_test.go, layout_test.go, look_test.go and frame_test.go do what the obligations say. The waived limits are still in the code as filed and are not filed again: the :root skip at stylesheet_test.go:233-236, the brace-free cssRuleRE, the owner signal assay that captures only the viewport, no planted pair, and no 320 px pass. Evidence from my first turn still stands: `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` exits 0 with CHROME_BIN set, Fitness holds all 45 rules, and gofmt and vet are clean. The run() and userInfo contract notes from that turn are already on this review under IN-m2 and IN-m1.

findings.claim: run() returns the serving *program.Program, but its Fake field is the stand-in program.Start made for itself, not the launcher's stand-in that the program is configured with (serveEnv sets HBAND_GITHUB_URL to the launcher's fake). So p.SignIn, p.Owner and p.Approve on run()'s result cannot work. Approve requires the login redirect to start with p.Fake.URL(), and SignIn calls SetUser on a fake nobody asks. Measured with a scratch overlay test: p.Fake.URL() was :62417 while /auth/github/login redirected to :62416, and p.Owner(t) fatalled with 'not a redirect to GitHub's authorize page'. Even with Fake repointed, SignIn would land on the picker's 200 page with no session cookie. No caller uses those methods today: main() and main_test.go discard the result, and screens_test uses only Anonymous(). Lesson #1007 tells later slices to reuse seeded's run(), though, and its doc comment does not warn that the returned Program cannot sign anyone in.
findings.evidence: main.go:211-224 builds the launcher's fake and passes it through Options.Env. program.Start still creates and returns its own fake (program.go:168, 205). visitor.go:89 and :123 use p.Fake. Overlay probe TestZZRunResultSignIn printed 'starts with p.Fake: false' and FAIL.

quote.text: final := program.Start(t, bin, program.Options{Port: n, Env: serveEnv})

findings.fix: Say in run()'s doc comment that the returned Program's Fake, SignIn, Owner and Approve do not reach the stand-in it signs in through, and that a caller signs in by following the picker as screens_test's signInBy does. Alternatively, return the launcher's *fakegithub.Fake alongside the Program.

findings.claim: This diff switched userInfo to report the picked account (id := fmt.Sprint(user.ID)), but the UserIDString and UserIDFloat switch arms still format f.user.ID, the SetUser account. When a picker choice is followed with either switch on, /user returns SetUser's ID (42 by default) instead of the chosen account's. That contradicts OfferChoices' doc ('approves that choice's account and nobody else'). No test or caller combines a switch with choices today.
findings.evidence: fakegithub.go:299-302 picks the user, :308 uses user.ID, and :313 and :315 still use f.user.ID.
findings.fix: Use user.ID in both arms: fmt.Sprintf("%q", fmt.Sprint(user.ID)) and fmt.Sprintf("%d.0", user.ID).

findings.claim: userFor's doc comment says it runs the exchange 'for the authorize request q', but the function has no q. Its parameter is authorizeURL, a full URL that it GETs.

quote.text: // userFor runs the whole exchange for the authorize request q (as a browser's

findings.fix: Change the comment to say 'for the authorize URL authorizeURL'.

findings.claim: checkStandIn's doc comment describes only the staging stand-in ('It was bound before the staging program'). This diff now also calls it at main.go:213 for the serving stand-in, which is bound before the serving program. Its failure messages (lines 236 and 240) still name 'the staging stand-in', so a collision on the serving stand-in would report the wrong one.

quote.text: // checkStandIn fails t when the stand-in GitHub at raw sits on port n. It was

findings.fix: Make the comment cover both callers, for example 'bound before the program it stands in for'. Optionally pass a name into the messages.

findings.claim: userInfo now answers with the picked account (`user := f.user; if picked != nil { user = *picked }`) for the id, login and avatar. The UserIDString and UserIDFloat switch cases still format `f.user.ID`, the account SetUser names. So when a test signs in through a picker link with either id-shape switch on, the stand-in reports the SetUser account's id. Measured: a picked owner 4242 comes back as id "42" (string) and as 42 (float), with the login report-author.
findings.evidence: fakegithub.go:308 `id := fmt.Sprint(user.ID)` was changed to the picked user, but :313 `id = fmt.Sprintf("%q", fmt.Sprint(f.user.ID))` and :315 `id = fmt.Sprintf("%d.0", f.user.ID)` were not. The scratch repro fails on 571ae37 and passes with both lines reading user.ID, and the whole fakegithub package stays green.
findings.fix: In userInfo, change `f.user.ID` to `user.ID` in the UserIDString and UserIDFloat cases.

quote.text:
case f.sw.UserIDString:
		id = fmt.Sprintf("%q", fmt.Sprint(f.user.ID))
	case f.sw.UserIDFloat:
		id = fmt.Sprintf("%d.0", f.user.ID)

findings.claim: run() now starts the serving program pointed at the launcher's own stand-in GitHub (HBAND_GITHUB_URL = fake.URL() through Options.Env). It returns `final`, whose Fake field is still the stand-in program.Start made for itself, which the serving program never asks. Every caller of the returned *program.Program that goes through p.Fake therefore talks to the wrong stand-in: p.SignIn and p.Owner call p.Fake.SetUser, Approve checks that the sign-in redirect starts with p.Fake.URL(), and p.Fake.TokenCalls counts there. Measured: the serving program redirected sign-in to http://127.0.0.1:52408/login/oauth/authorize while the returned p.Fake.URL() was http://127.0.0.1:52409. Before this build the returned Program's Fake was the one its program used.
findings.evidence: main.go:211-222 builds `fake := fakegithub.New(...)` and starts `final := program.Start(t, bin, program.Options{Port: n, Env: serveEnv})`. program.go:168 and :205 set Program.Fake to Start's own `fake`, and childEnv lets Options.Env override HBAND_GITHUB_URL/API_URL. The scratch repro fails on 571ae37 and passes once `final.Fake = fake` is added. TestSeededProductOffersTheOwnerAndTheReader and the whole seeded package still pass with that change.
findings.fix: In run(), after `final := program.Start(...)`, set `final.Fake = fake`, so the returned Program names the stand-in its program signs in through. Alternatively, document that the returned Program's Fake and SignIn must not be used.

quote.text:

	return final

obligations.evidence: internal/server/look_test.go TestEveryScreenIsDesigned emulates prefers-color-scheme dark on every state, and probe.js asserts every check plus a background that differs between schemes. Verified in my attempts 2 and 3. The files are unchanged in f83e789..571ae37.

probe.js compares scrollWidth with the requested width and asserts innerWidth == 375 on mobile. The look test seeds /admin/reports/x (SHA-256 dd), /admin (5-column table, file input) and a 39-character login. Files unchanged since my attempt 3.

look_test.go runs a details-open pass on the owner report, admin report and populated Blocked users pages, and on Reply at the cap. The role rows require the danger fill on the .remove/.block confirms. Unchanged.
look_test.go captures the owner states in both schemes with details open and runs headless.Count for #ff0000/#00ff00. The capture is viewport-only, which is the limitation waived as O-028.
branch_test.go TestStaticThreadScript passes in the full suite I ran (exit 0). base.html gates thread.js on .ThreadScript, and reader.go overrides it on readerData.

probe.js checks that #feedback-sent has no client rects unless the hash targets it (reached via about:blank), and that re-hidden .toggle computes display none. site.css keeps [hidden]:not(:target). Unchanged.
TestThreadFitsPhoneWidth passes in my full-suite run. probe.js asserts at least one depth-5 .body of 240 px or more on the branch page at 360 and 375, with a 12-level seed.
frame_test.go TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas, report A light: frame equals standalone. site.css iframe has background-color: Canvas. Unchanged; it passed in my full-suite run.
Same test, report B dark: #204060 both inside the frame and alone. No color-scheme below :root (lintStylesheet). Unchanged.
Same test, report C in both schemes equals standalone (#ffffff, #121212). Unchanged.

internal/auth/forbidden_test.go TestForbiddenPageTakesTheShell covers '' and 'octo<b>&cat': title, one site.css link, sentence, escaped login, brand, no marker, no script. It passed in the full suite.
look_test.go: the refused-upload state is a real Chrome POST through headless.Tab.Submit with noValidate and an invalid slug. It asserts p.error[role=alert], then probes. Unchanged.
stylesheet_test.go TestStylesheetTokens and TestStylesheetCorpus pass. The pair fault shape has no planted test, which is waived as O-029.
internal/layout/layout_test.go TestEveryPageTakesTheShell plus TestShellCheckerSeesEachFault pass in the full suite.
The builder measured TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas with a non-canvas --bg, and removing Canvas failed 4 of 6 cases. The frame rule is unchanged in this build.

probe.js measures rendered contrast on every visible text and control, including forced :hover and :focus-visible, and the run passes. The limit is states outside the seed and engines other than Chrome. Unchanged.

Open and owed to validate-slice. light-dark(), the frame Canvas and the avatar cover were measured only in Chrome 158, because Firefox and Safari are not on this machine. Build 4 did not touch it, and nothing in the tree measures another engine.

probe.js fit check against the requested width and innerWidth. TestLookProbeSeesTheStylesheetBeforeTheDesign serves testdata/look/site.before.css and requires a fit violation. It passed in the full suite.
probe.js judges only painted properties. The same sensitivity test flags link, button, input, select, textarea, th and td on the pre-slice stylesheet. Unchanged.

internal/testutil/headless/devtools.go Tab.Submit drains loads, evaluates once and waits on the load channel, and every state starts from about:blank. TestTabSubmitWaitsForTheRedirectedPage passes in the headless package run.
probe.js computes depth as 1 + the number of .replies ancestors, asserts the cap body is 240 px or more, and records atCap. The branch page is taken from the continue href. Unchanged.
lintStylesheet named-colour and function scan with stylesheet_corpus.json colour-literal rows. The :root member gap is still in the code and was carried to SC-059/SC-061 (O-027/O-031).
lintStylesheet strips vendor prefixes and bans filter, backdrop-filter, mix-blend-mode, opacity, mask* and clip-path anywhere. The nested-rule gap was carried to SC-060 (O-030).
site.css edges are written as a literal width and style followed by a *-color token longhand, and :focus-visible uses outline-color. lintStylesheet refuses var() in an edge shorthand. Unchanged.
look_test.go forces :hover and :focus-visible through CSS.forcePseudoState and re-runs contrast, and the static pair table has a coverage check. Unchanged.
layout_test.go matches script case-insensitively across internal/**/templates and pins base.html to the one gated thread.js tag. Unchanged.
Waived to SC-059. stylesheet_test.go's :root branch still skips ordinary properties, and nothing changed it in this build.
Waived to note N-255. The owner assay still uses the viewport-only shoot in look_test.go. Unchanged.
Waived to note N-256. There is still no test planting a below-bar pair.
Waived to SC-060. cssRuleRE is still brace-free, so declarations beside a nested rule are not linted.
Waived to SC-061. This is the same :root skip as O-027, still in the code.
Waived to note N-254. site.css is unchanged in this build, and no 320 px admin pass was added.
